status: draft-v4 (internal assistive; a human reviewer is the final authority)

defaults.perspective_preference: One-way (unilateral) with Amperesand Inc as the sole Disclosing Party and the individual (a natural person) as Receiving Party; this favorable one-sidedness is INTENTIONAL because Amperesand discloses confidential business/product/IP information to an individual (e.g., a prospective advisor, consultant, candidate, or counterparty being assessed for a business opportunity) who discloses little or nothing back.
defaults.forum: AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat in Nevada, USA, conducted in English; court carve-out permitting either party (in practice the Disclosing Party / Amperesand) to seek specific performance or injunctive/equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.
defaults.term_standard: Agreement term: one (1) year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice (template Clause 8).
defaults.survival_standard: Template Clause 8 states each Party's rights and obligations survive any termination or expiration but sets NO finite period (drafting defect). Adopted internal default per the internal uNDA-Individual survival recommendation: 5 years per disclosure for ordinary Confidential Information + an uncapped trade-secret tail (as long as it remains a trade secret under DTSA / applicable state UTSA), measured from each disclosure (rolling), with a 3-year pre-authorized fallback. Pending counsel refinement.
required_carveouts: prior_possession (already in the Receiving Party's possession or known to it before disclosure)
public_domain (is or comes into the public domain through no fault or breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party)
third_party (received from a third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality in disclosing the same)
independent_development (independently developed by the Receiving Party without regard or reference to the Confidential Information)
written_authorization (approved for release or use by written authorization of the Disclosing Party)
counsel_must_confirm: ADOPTED (pending counsel): the uNDA Clause 4 -> Clause 8 cross-reference sets no finite survival period (template defect). Adopted default: 5yr per-disclosure ordinary CI + uncapped trade-secret tail, 3yr fallback (internal survival recommendation, which expressly applies to the individual uNDA template).
ADOPTED (pending counsel): an uncapped/perpetual trade-secret carve-out is the standard survival default; confirm approved drafting language.

ADOPTED (pending counsel): individual-enforceability realism — against a natural person, equitable relief (injunction / specific performance) and the return/destruction obligation are the practically meaningful remedies; large monetary recovery and arbitration cost-recovery may be limited by the individual's resources. Confirm whether to add a streamlined low-cost dispute path for individual counterparties.

ADOPTED (pending counsel): personal_data_privacy — template Clause 1(e) sweeps 'any shared personal data' into Confidential Information; on US/Delaware paper this is governed by general confidentiality + applicable US privacy law, NOT PDPA. Confirm no foreign (Singapore PDPA / Companies Act / Electronic Transactions Act) references leak into this US-to-US agreement.
RESOLVED: US/Amperesand Inc forum = AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat Nevada (template Clause 16, template-true). Delaware-seated arrangements are drift, demoted to fallback.
RESOLVED: compelled disclosure is a separate Required-Disclosure-with-notice clause (template Clause 3), not the 5th definitional exclusion (which is written-authorization).
RESOLVED: injunctive/equitable-relief court carve-out is the standard default alongside arbitration (template Clause 12 + Clause 16).

STANDING (individual-specific): the template's 'Affiliate' definition (Clause 15) applies ONLY to the Disclosing Party (Amperesand) — an individual Receiving Party has no affiliates/group. Do NOT add affiliate-disclosure or group-sharing rights for the individual; keep the disclosee universe limited to the individual personally (plus, at most, a narrow need-to-know professional-advisor carve-out the individual remains responsible for).

STANDING (individual-specific): the individual's government-ID identifier must be completed (last four digits only per template) and the notice block filled before execution; never sign with placeholder name/ID/address fields.

STANDING (per-deal): this type has no executed examples; if an individual counterparty proposes their own paper or redlines Amperesand's, run the fallback ladders below. Default expectation is the individual signs Amperesand paper as presented.

positions.title: Definition of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information is defined broadly as any and all information relating to the Purpose, disclosed, furnished or communicated in writing or orally by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party (Amperesand) to the Receiving Party (the individual) or to an authorized third party acting on the individual's behalf, which is marked or communicated as confidential, PLUS a catch-all sweeping in unmarked information that is reasonably apparent to someone familiar with the subject area as the type typically treated as confidential (or that the Receiving Party has reason to believe may be confidential). It expressly covers: the existence/terms of the Agreement and the negotiations; Amperesand's business, affairs, business opportunities, customers, clients, suppliers, plans, intentions and market opportunities (and those of its Affiliates and contemplated subsidiaries); its IP, operations, processes, product information, know-how, technical information, designs, trade secrets and software (and those of its Affiliates / future portfolio companies); derived data/analyses; any shared personal data; and third-party confidential information held by Amperesand. No oral-to-writing confirmation deadline and no marking requirement to qualify. NOTE the template asymmetry: 'Affiliate' (Clause 15) is defined and expands the DISCLOSING party's (Amperesand's) protected information only — the individual Receiving Party has no affiliate/group whose information is brought into scope. (Template Clause 1.)
walk_away_triggers: Adding a marking/legending requirement or an oral-to-writing memorialization deadline (e.g., must confirm in writing within 15-30 days) as a precondition to protection — strips protection from Amperesand's unmarked oral/visual disclosures, which are common when briefing an individual advisor/consultant/candidate.

Narrowing the definition so it only protects information formally 'delivered' to or expressly accepted by the individual, leaving Amperesand's broader shared information (financials, roadmaps, customer/supplier identities, designs shown in a meeting) outside scope.

Converting the one-way definition into a mutual/reciprocal one that auto-deems the individual's own materials or ideas as that individual's Confidential Information — the intended design is Amperesand as SOLE discloser; resist reciprocity unless the individual genuinely discloses protectable information back.
Inserting an affiliate/group-sharing limb for the individual (an individual has no affiliates) that would let information be deemed shared with, or disclosed to, undefined associated persons.
Burden-of-proof-on-the-discloser language requiring Amperesand to prove information qualifies as confidential, combined with deletion of the 'reasonably apparent / reason to believe' catch-all.

Embedding foreign (e.g., Singapore PDPA / Companies Act) statutory definitions into this Delaware-governed US agreement, creating jurisdictional ambiguity over the personal-data and related-corporation concepts — clean out before signing.
acceptable_fallbacks: Adding a confidentiality legend/marking PRACTICE for documents while preserving protection for oral/visual disclosures and retaining the 'reasonably apparent / reason to believe' catch-all (no hard memorialization deadline).

A symmetric mutual definition ONLY where the engagement genuinely involves the individual disclosing protectable information back (rare for an individual), provided Amperesand's broad scope is preserved unchanged.

Excluding the existence/terms-of-Agreement limb only where the individual must disclose the relationship to a regulator or to obtain professional advice, replaced by a need-to-know permitted-disclosure right.

positions.title: Purpose Limitation
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information may be used by the individual solely for the single, narrowly defined 'Purpose' stated in the recitals — Amperesand evaluating the capabilities of the individual with respect to the assessment of a business opportunity of interest to Amperesand, and the individual receiving certain information in order to demonstrate those capabilities — and for no other purpose. (Template recitals + Clause 4.)
walk_away_triggers: Individual-side purpose expansion permitting use of Amperesand's CI for the individual's other clients/employers, the individual's own ventures or personal investment decisions, or to improve the individual's general expertise/portfolio beyond the specific assessment — enables Amperesand's information to bleed into the individual's other work.

Anti-reverse-engineering or 'design-around' prohibition drafted broadly enough to constrain Amperesand's own legitimate independent engineering (Amperesand should never be use-restricted on its own paper as discloser; resist if reciprocated onto Amperesand).

Leaving the Purpose as an unfilled bracketed placeholder in the executed copy (the template recital carries bracketed alternative language) — finalize to a single complete Purpose before signing to avoid scope ambiguity.

Open-ended catch-all extending permitted use to 'business activities arising from the relationship' or 'other purposes as the parties may agree,' converting an evaluation NDA into a standing personal-use license without a definitive engagement agreement.
acceptable_fallbacks: Describing the Purpose to cover both the capability assessment AND performance of a specifically named follow-on engagement (so a single NDA spans the relationship) provided it stays tied to the specific business opportunity.

A narrow, mutual reverse-engineering restriction limited to genuine misappropriation of the specific disclosed CI, with an express carve-in for Amperesand's pre-existing and independently developed work.

positions.title: Exclusions from Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Five standard exclusions, borne by the Receiving Party (the individual): (a) already in the individual's possession or known to the individual before disclosure; (b) is or comes into the public domain through no fault or breach of the Agreement by the individual; (c) received from a third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality in disclosing it; (d) independently developed by the individual without regard or reference to the Confidential Information; (e) approved for release or use by written authorization of the Disclosing Party. Compelled disclosure is handled separately as Required Disclosure (Clause 3), NOT as an exclusion. (Template Clause 2.)
walk_away_triggers: Broadening the independent-development carve-out so the individual can claim anything later created was 'independently developed,' or dropping the 'without regard or reference to the Confidential Information' qualifier — lets the individual launder Amperesand's information into 'their own' work.
A public-domain carve-out drafted as 'whatever later becomes public' without the 'through no fault or breach by the Receiving Party' qualifier, rewarding the individual's own leaks.

Adding exclusions beyond the five standard ones (e.g., 'information of a general nature,' 'residuals,' 'information retained in memory') that erode protection of Amperesand's disclosed CI — an especially acute leakage risk against a memory-carrying individual.
Recasting compelled disclosure as a 6th blanket exclusion (removing the notice/minimization/confidential-treatment obligations of the separate Required Disclosure clause).
acceptable_fallbacks: Tightening the third-party carve-out to require the third party be 'not known by the Receiving Party to be under' a confidentiality obligation (knowledge qualifier) — acceptable as it favors Amperesand as discloser.
Express statement that the burden of proving an exclusion rests on the Receiving Party (favors Amperesand).

positions.title: Confidentiality Obligations of the Receiving Party
positions.standard_position: At all times, and notwithstanding any termination or expiration, the individual must hold Amperesand's CI in strict confidence and not disclose it to any third party without Amperesand's prior written approval; use it for no purpose other than the Purpose; apply at least the same degree of precaution it uses for its own confidential information of like importance but in no event less than reasonable care; not copy, reduce to writing or otherwise record the CI except as strictly necessary for the Purpose (such copies, reductions and records being Amperesand's property); and immediately notify Amperesand upon discovery of any loss or unauthorized disclosure. The Agreement also imposes No Publicity (Clause 5): no public release or announcement by the individual without Amperesand's prior written approval. Because the Receiving Party is a natural person, the obligation runs DIRECTLY to the individual — there is no entity 'Representatives' set and no affiliate/group sharing. (Template Clauses 4 and 5.)
walk_away_triggers: Diluting the care standard below reasonable care, or making the confidentiality obligation expire with the agreement term rather than surviving (the template's Clause 4 'at all times and notwithstanding any termination or expiration' language must be preserved, subject to the Clause 8 survival period).

Inserting a need-to-know 'Representatives' or affiliate-sharing carve-out for the individual that lets the individual route Amperesand's CI to colleagues, co-investors, family members, or a firm the individual works for, without Amperesand's consent — an individual has no entity group and must not acquire one by drafting.
Deleting the 'copies are Disclosing Party's property' / 'not copy except as strictly necessary' limb so the individual may freely reproduce Amperesand's materials.
Removing the immediate loss/unauthorized-disclosure notification obligation or the No Publicity restriction (Clause 5).

On flipped/counterparty paper where the individual's form makes Amperesand the receiver: a mandatory affirmative obligation to litigate at Amperesand's own cost, a requirement that each Amperesand person individually sign undertakings before access, or an AI-training prohibition / one-sided cybersecurity-audit-and-remediation-at-Amperesand's-expense regime bolted on — push back or reciprocate.
acceptable_fallbacks: A narrow need-to-know carve-out permitting the individual to disclose ONLY to the individual's own legal/tax advisor bound by professional confidentiality, with the individual remaining fully responsible for that advisor's compliance.
A 'commercially reasonable' notification window (e.g., within 2-3 business days) in place of 'immediately' for loss/unauthorized-disclosure notice.
Adding an express undertaking that the individual will not use any AI tool or third-party service that would transmit Amperesand's CI outside the individual's control.

positions.title: Permitted Disclosures (Compelled Only)
positions.standard_position: For an individual Receiving Party the template grants essentially ONE permitted disclosure: where compelled by a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority with jurisdiction (Clause 3), provided the individual (i) gives Amperesand reasonable prior written notice (to the extent legally permitted), (ii) discloses only the minimum required, and (iii) uses reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment, with prompt post-hoc notice if advance notice was impossible. Unlike the entity types, there is NO 'Representatives' need-to-know disclosure limb — a natural person has no organization to share within; any sharing requires Amperesand's prior written approval (Clause 4). (Template Clause 3; cf. Clause 4.)
walk_away_triggers: Granting the individual a standing right to disclose to colleagues, an employer/firm, co-investors, financing sources, or family members without Amperesand's consent and without a compulsion trigger — manufactures an entity-style disclosee universe for a natural person.
Removing the prior-notice / minimization / confidential-treatment obligations from the compelled-disclosure mechanism, or removing the compelled-disclosure clause entirely.
A standing third-party (e.g., the individual's employer or a regulator) inspection or pass-through right not tied to actual legal compulsion.
Long fixed advance-notice periods (e.g., 30 days) for compelled disclosure that cannot be met under urgent orders.
acceptable_fallbacks: A narrow need-to-know carve-out adding the individual's own legal/tax advisor to a permitted-disclosee set, provided that advisor is bound by professional or contractual confidentiality and the individual remains fully responsible.
A 'to the extent legally permitted' notice standard (rather than absolute notice) on compelled disclosure — already the template position and acceptable.

positions.title: Required (Compelled) Disclosure
positions.standard_position: If the individual is obligated or requested to disclose Amperesand's CI under a valid order of a court or any governmental body or regulatory authority having jurisdiction, the individual shall (i) provide Amperesand with reasonable prior written notice of such disclosure, (ii) disclose only such CI as is required by the relevant order/authority, and (iii) use reasonable efforts to ensure the CI disclosed is accorded confidential treatment; if unable to notify Amperesand before disclosure, the individual shall, to the extent permitted by law, inform Amperesand of the full circumstances and the information disclosed as soon as reasonably practicable. (Template Clause 3.)
walk_away_triggers: Deletion of the prior-written-notice obligation, the minimization ('only such CI required') obligation, or the confidential-treatment-efforts obligation.

Shifting onto Amperesand (as discloser) the cost or sole burden of resisting/limiting the individual's compelled disclosure as a baseline term, or requiring Amperesand to take 'all steps the individual may require' to fight the order.
Treating compelled disclosure as an outright exclusion that ends all obligations rather than a narrow, notice-bound permitted disclosure.
acceptable_fallbacks: Replacing 'reasonable prior written notice' with 'prompt notice to the extent legally permitted' where a protective order or gag applies.
Permitting disclosure to a regulator under a routine, recurring legal obligation provided confidential-treatment efforts and post-hoc notice are preserved.

positions.title: Term of the Agreement
positions.standard_position: The Agreement commences on the Effective Date and expires one (1) year from the Effective Date, subject to earlier termination by either Party on written notice (Clause 9). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, each Party's rights and obligations survive any termination or expiration. (Template Clause 8.)
walk_away_triggers: Individual-imposed perpetual/evergreen term with no fixed expiry that survives indefinitely absent affirmative notice (resist; if accepted, retain a short termination-for-convenience right).
Removing the bilateral early-termination-on-notice right, locking Amperesand into the full term with no exit.
A term tied to or floored by an underlying engagement/consulting agreement (e.g., multi-year minimums) with no independent NDA termination right.
Internal word/numeral contradiction in the term figure (spelled-out number disagreeing with the parenthetical) — correct before signature.
acceptable_fallbacks: A 2-3 year agreement term matched to the expected length of the relationship/engagement, provided the bilateral termination-on-notice right is retained.
A term that auto-renews annually but remains terminable on notice by either party.

positions.title: Survival of Confidentiality Obligations
positions.standard_position: Confidentiality rights and obligations survive any termination or expiration of the Agreement (template Clause 8 'will survive'; reinforced by Clause 4 'at all times and notwithstanding any termination or expiration'), but the template sets NO finite survival period (drafting defect). Adopted internal default per the internal uNDA survival recommendation (which expressly applies to the individual uNDA template): ordinary Confidential Information protected for 5 years per disclosure (3-year pre-authorized fallback); trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets under DTSA / applicable state UTSA (uncapped); measured from the date of each disclosure (rolling, per-item), NOT the Effective Date. Pending counsel refinement.
walk_away_triggers: No post-termination survival at all, or confidentiality co-terminous with the (1-year) agreement term — leaves Amperesand's disclosed CI unprotected once the short term ends.
A finite survival cap on trade secrets (e.g., 'all obligations end after N years' with no trade-secret tail) when Amperesand is disclosing trade-secret-grade IP to the individual.
Survival anchored to the Effective Date with a period equal to or shorter than the agreement term, producing zero or near-zero effective post-expiry tail.
Internally contradictory survival drafting a court could read as expiring with the agreement, or a word/numeral mismatch — fix before signing.
acceptable_fallbacks: 3 years per disclosure for ordinary CI (the pre-authorized fallback) PLUS the uncapped trade-secret tail.
Survival re-anchored to termination/expiry (rather than the Effective Date) to lengthen the post-expiry tail, with the trade-secret tail preserved.

Against an individual, accepting a somewhat shorter ordinary-CI tail in exchange for an enforceable, clearly drafted trade-secret tail is acceptable where enforcement realism (limited individual resources) argues for the trade-secret protection being the operative safeguard.

positions.title: Return or Destruction of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Within fourteen (14) days of (i) Amperesand's written request (per Clause 9) or (ii) expiration/termination, the individual must return to Amperesand or destroy all documents and other tangible materials representing Amperesand's CI and all copies, except the individual may retain one (1) copy (including electronic records/files created pursuant to automatic archiving/back-up) solely to perform surviving obligations and for so long as required by law, court, regulatory authority, or the individual's internal audit/compliance procedures; the Agreement continues to apply to any retained copy. (Template Clause 7.)
walk_away_triggers: Retention satisfied by reference to the individual's (or the individual's firm's) own record-retention or document-governance policy rather than a specific legal requirement — lets the individual keep Amperesand's CI as long as a policy allows, rendering the destroy obligation illusory.
Open-ended/indefinite retention of backup/archival copies with no sunset and no continuing confidentiality tail on retained copies.
A broad carve-out letting the individual retain derivative work product (notes, analyses, summaries) derived from Amperesand's CI.
Return-only with no destruction option and no certification mechanism, or loss of Amperesand's right to demand return on demand at any time.
acceptable_fallbacks: A modestly longer return/destruction window (e.g., 30 days) to accommodate the individual's personal IT/back-up cycle.
A written certification of destruction in lieu of physical return for electronically stored CI.
Retention of the single archival copy under the template's narrow legal/compliance purpose, with the Agreement continuing to govern it (already the template position).

positions.title: No Transfer of Rights, Title, or Interest
positions.standard_position: Amperesand (the Disclosing Party) retains all of its rights in its Confidential Information (including any copies or extracts) and grants no licenses or rights to any Confidential Information except those expressly set forth in the Agreement; nothing in the Agreement is intended to grant a license to, or waive any rights in, any patents, copyrights, trademarks or mask works belonging to Amperesand. (Template Clause 10.)
walk_away_triggers: Any IP-assignment, vesting, or work-for-hire obligation requiring Amperesand to assign or transfer ownership of IP, inventions, or 'derivatives of Confidential Information' to the individual — an NDA must not become an IP-transfer instrument.
A clause purporting to grant the individual a license to Amperesand's IP, or deeming disclosure an implied license/waiver of Amperesand's patents/copyrights/trademarks/mask works.

A patent-filing prohibition barring Amperesand from filing on information exchanged, or 'derived directly or indirectly / in the course of interaction' IP-capture language that sweeps in Amperesand's own innovations.

Any clause vesting in the individual ownership of ideas, feedback, notes, or improvements the individual generates from exposure to Amperesand's CI, with no assignment or license back to Amperesand (if the individual will create deliverables, allocate IP in a separate consulting/services agreement — NOT this NDA).
acceptable_fallbacks: A neutral statement that each party retains its own pre-existing IP (acceptable since Amperesand is the primary discloser).

If the individual is being engaged to advise or create, deferring any work-product/feedback IP ownership expressly to a separate consulting agreement (preferred), with the NDA silent on vesting and creating no ownership rights in the individual.

positions.title: No Warranty / No Other Obligations (AS-IS)
positions.standard_position: Nothing in the Agreement compels Amperesand to supply any or all CI requested (Amperesand may decline at its discretion) or to enter into any transaction; no partnership, joint venture or agency is created between the parties; either party may at any time, in its sole discretion, terminate discussions and negotiations. By implication the CI is provided without representation or warranty as to accuracy/completeness and Amperesand bears no liability for the individual's use or reliance. (Template Clause 6; consider adding an express AS-IS disclaimer.)
walk_away_triggers: An affirmative warranty extracted from Amperesand (accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, fitness, performance of its CI) beyond the narrow right to disclose.

A consequential/indirect/punitive damages waiver or liability cap bundled in that would limit Amperesand's recovery when the individual misuses or improperly discloses its CI — if it must remain, carve out confidentiality breaches and IP misappropriation.
A no-warranty clause coupled with an indemnity by Amperesand for the individual's use of/reliance on disclosed information (indemnity in an NDA is dealbreaker-class).
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual AS-IS / no-reliance disclaimer (acceptable and protective of Amperesand as discloser).
A mutual limitation excluding consequential damages provided confidentiality breaches and IP misappropriation are expressly carved out of the limitation.

positions.title: Remedies / Injunctive Relief
positions.standard_position: Each Party acknowledges monetary damages alone may not be a sufficient remedy for a breach and agrees Amperesand (as Disclosing Party) is entitled to seek specific performance or injunctive relief from any court in any jurisdiction, in addition to all other remedies available to it (template Clause 12). Also relevant is the No-Waiver clause (Clause 11). Against an INDIVIDUAL, equitable relief and the return/destruction obligation are the practically meaningful remedies — large monetary recovery may be limited by the individual's resources — so the injunctive-relief acknowledgment is the load-bearing term for this type.
walk_away_triggers: Deleting the injunctive-relief / irreparable-harm acknowledgment (template Clause 12), leaving Amperesand without an express equitable remedy — especially damaging here because equitable relief is the most effective remedy against a natural person.
Requiring Amperesand to post a bond, or imposing a fixed/nominal bond cap, as a precondition to injunctive relief.
Narrowing injunctive relief to IP-infringement only, excluding ordinary confidentiality breaches.
Prevailing-party attorneys'-fee shifting bolted on (not in Amperesand's template), which asymmetrically deters enforcement.
On flipped/counterparty paper: a blanket pre-emptive waiver requiring Amperesand (as recipient) to not oppose injunctive relief.
acceptable_fallbacks: Making the injunctive-relief right mutual (either party as discloser) — acceptable and consistent with the template's reciprocal-acknowledgment framing.
Specifying that injunctive relief is sought in a court of competent jurisdiction notwithstanding the arbitration clause (clarifies the carve-out).
Adding a simple, low-cost enforcement path (e.g., expedited interim relief) appropriate to an individual counterparty's resources.

positions.title: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
positions.standard_position: Governed and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware. Any disputes arising out of or in connection with the Agreement are referred to arbitration by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat in Nevada, USA. A court carve-out for specific performance / injunctive/equitable relief applies via the remedies clause. (Template Clause 16 + Clause 12.)
walk_away_triggers: Replacing Delaware law / AAA-Nevada arbitration with the individual's home-state or home-country law and forum, giving the counterparty home-court advantage — particularly a foreign individual's local courts.
Specifying governing law but no forum/dispute mechanism, or a forum but no governing law.
An internally contradictory forum clause naming two incompatible institutions or seats in one provision (risk of a void clause).
Litigation in the individual's home courts with prevailing-party fee-shifting to the individual.

Ambiguous choice-of-law ('internal laws of the United States') without a named state, or embedding foreign statutory references (e.g., Singapore PDPA / Companies Act / Electronic Transactions Act) in this Delaware-governed agreement.
acceptable_fallbacks: AAA arbitration seated in Delaware (rather than Nevada) — observed drift; acceptable fallback, not the standard.
A neutral US state's law and seat where a foreign individual resists Delaware/Nevada, provided arbitration (not the individual's home courts) is retained.

Given that AAA Commercial Arbitration can be cost-disproportionate for an individual, accepting AAA Consumer/streamlined rules or a neutral US-court litigation forum on a per-deal basis where it improves practical enforceability against the individual.

positions.title: Assignment
positions.standard_position: Neither Party may assign any of its rights or delegate any of its obligations without the other Party's prior written consent, except that (i) Amperesand (Disclosing Party) may assign its rights and delegate its obligations to any person or entity that acquires substantially all of Amperesand's assets directly or by operation of law, and (ii) Amperesand may assign the Agreement to any Affiliate. Any purported assignment in violation is null and void; assignment does not relieve the assigning Party of its obligations; the Agreement is for the sole benefit of the parties and their successors and permitted assigns and confers no rights on any other person. (Template Clause 15.)
walk_away_triggers: Granting the individual a right to assign or delegate the Agreement (or to transfer access to Amperesand's CI to a firm, employer, or third party) without Amperesand's consent — for a natural person the obligation should be personal and non-assignable.
A 'binding on successors and assigns' clause with no consent requirement, allowing automatic assignment by either side.

Making the assignment restriction one-sided against Amperesand while leaving the individual free to assign (the template's intentional one-sidedness runs the OTHER way — in Amperesand's favor, via the Affiliate/asset-sale carve-outs).
Deleting Amperesand's Affiliate / asset-sale assignment carve-outs.
Removing the assignment clause entirely, defaulting to permissive local-law assignment rules.
acceptable_fallbacks: Confirming expressly that the individual's obligations are personal and non-assignable (favors Amperesand).

Mutualizing the asset-sale carve-out is generally inapt for an individual; if pressed, limit any individual-side assignment to operation of law (e.g., the individual's estate) with the assignee bound by the NDA and Amperesand's consent for anything else.

positions.title: Residuals (No Residuals Clause)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO residuals clause and no competitive-use carve-out; the individual must keep CI confidential and use it solely for the Purpose, with no right to use memory-retained 'residuals' or to apply Amperesand's CI to other clients/employers, the individual's own ventures, or competing development.
walk_away_triggers: A residuals clause permitting the individual to use information retained in unaided memory for any purpose — an especially serious leakage vector against a natural person who carries knowledge between engagements/employers.
A competitive-use or 'general experience/skill' carve-out letting the individual apply Amperesand's CI to advise or work for Amperesand's competitors.
Any residuals / 'skills and experience' clause lacking an express prohibition on direct use of Amperesand's CI.
acceptable_fallbacks: If the individual insists, a narrowly cabined residuals concept limited to genuinely unaided memory AND expressly excluding any use that competes with Amperesand or applies its specific CI/trade secrets — documented as a counterparty-paper fallback only, never Amperesand-standard.
Reject residuals entirely (preferred); the template's clean Purpose-limited model is the standard.

positions.title: Non-Solicitation (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO standalone non-solicitation covenant; an NDA is a confidentiality instrument, not a trade-restraint vehicle. An inserted non-solicit is treated as prohibited, high-severity, and walk-away-class (a narrow, use-tethered, mutual non-solicit may be entertained only as a documented counterparty-paper fallback).
walk_away_triggers: Any standalone non-solicitation covenant untethered from use of Confidential Information.
A non-solicit binding only Amperesand (one-way against the discloser), or exceeding 12 months / perpetual.
A non-solicit lacking a general-advertising / non-targeted-recruiting carve-out.
A customer/supplier non-solicit broad enough to restrain Amperesand's ordinary business (de facto non-compete).
Liquidated damages or indemnity tied to a non-solicit breach.
acceptable_fallbacks: A narrow, mutual, time-limited (<=12 months) no-poach with a public-advertising carve-out — documented as a counterparty-paper fallback only.
Deletion (preferred).

positions.title: Non-Competition (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's NDA template contains NO non-competition clause; an NDA should remain a confidentiality instrument only. Preferred position: no non-compete, no non-compete-taint restriction, and no non-compete waiver in either direction.
walk_away_triggers: Any non-compete or 'residual contamination'/taint restriction barring Amperesand personnel exposed to the individual's information from working on competing technology — a de facto non-compete on Amperesand's engineering teams.
A broad 'competes' definition tied to a personnel-segregation/taint obligation that could sterilize Amperesand's R&D roadmap.
A non-compete waiver extracted from Amperesand acknowledging the individual may serve Amperesand's competitors, with no reciprocal confidentiality/use safeguards.
Any actual restraint on Amperesand competing, embedded in the NDA.
acceptable_fallbacks: Deletion (preferred).

If the individual seeks acknowledgment that they advise/work for others, a narrow statement that the individual may do so provided they do not use or disclose Amperesand's CI — with no taint/segregation obligation on Amperesand.

positions.title: Indemnification (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's standard NDA contains NO indemnification, hold-harmless, or fee-shifting provision; confidentiality breaches are remedied through general-law damages and equitable relief. Preferred position: strike any indemnity or attorneys'-fees clause.
walk_away_triggers: An indemnity running against Amperesand (as discloser) for the individual's use of/reliance on disclosed information, or any uncapped one-way indemnity.
Legal costs recoverable on a solicitor-client / 'indemnity basis' rather than reasonable party-and-party costs.
Indemnity/liability extending to 'attempted or threatened' disclosure and to a broad indemnitee list.
Any non-mutual fee-shifting or indemnity running only in the individual's favor.
Indemnity lacking carve-outs aligned to the confidentiality exclusions and compelled disclosure.
acceptable_fallbacks: If unavoidable, a mutual indemnity capped and excluding indirect/consequential loss, limited to third-party claims arising from a confidentiality breach — documented as a counterparty-paper fallback only.
Deletion (preferred).

positions.title: Personal Data / Privacy (Individual-Specific; US framing)
positions.standard_position: The template (Clause 1(e)) sweeps 'any shared personal data' into the definition of Confidential Information, so personal data Amperesand shares with the individual is protected on the same strict-confidence / Purpose-limited / return-or-destroy basis as all other CI. Because this is a US/Delaware agreement, personal-data handling is governed by general confidentiality plus APPLICABLE US privacy law — NOT Singapore PDPA. The individual is the data RECIPIENT; Amperesand does not, by this NDA, assume controller/processor obligations toward the individual beyond confidentiality. Conversely, any personal data of the individual that Amperesand collects (e.g., the individual's name and government-ID last-four in the preamble/notices) is handled under Amperesand's own privacy practices.
walk_away_triggers: A full PDPA (Singapore) personal-data clause, or other foreign privacy-law obligations, imported into this US/Delaware agreement — creates governing-law conflict; clean out before signing (use US framing).

A privacy/data-protection regime imposing controller-grade obligations, breach-notification timelines, audit rights, or processing restrictions on AMPERESAND as a precondition to sharing — out of scope for a one-way NDA where Amperesand is the discloser; resist or scope-limit.

The individual demanding broad rights over, or refusing confidentiality treatment of, personal data Amperesand shares (e.g., to onward-share with the individual's employer), undercutting Clause 1(e) protection.
Collection of more of the individual's sensitive identifiers than necessary (the template deliberately limits the government-ID reference to the last four digits) — do not expand.
acceptable_fallbacks: A short, mutual data-handling acknowledgment stating each party will handle the other's shared personal data confidentially and in accordance with applicable US law, with no foreign-statute references.
A US breach-notification courtesy obligation (prompt notice of any unauthorized disclosure of shared personal data) — consistent with the existing immediate-notification duty in Clause 4.
Limiting any privacy undertaking to the personal data actually shared for the Purpose, on a need-to-know basis.

positions.title: Notices, Waiver, Severability, Counterparts, E-Signature
positions.standard_position: Notices effective on delivery by hand, or by email or certified/registered mail (return receipt requested) to the specified addresses (Amperesand's designated notice contacts). Clean boilerplate: No Waiver (Clause 11), Severability (Clause 13), and Counterparts / PDF-or-electronic-signature execution (Clause 17) recognizing Adobe Sign/DocuSign as original signatures. The individual's full name, government-ID last-four identifier, address and email must be completed before execution. (Template Clauses 9, 11, 13, 17.)
walk_away_triggers: Leaving the individual's name, identifier, address, or email as blank/placeholder fields in the executed agreement — never sign with placeholder notice/identity details, as it undermines valid service and counterparty identification.
Embedding foreign (Singapore) statutory references (PDPA, Companies Act, Electronic Transactions Act) in this Delaware/US-governed agreement — clean out.
An attorneys'-fee / prevailing-party fee-shifting clause inserted (not in Amperesand's standard).
A unilateral right for the individual to transfer the NDA and all received CI to a third party (e.g., an employer) without consent/notice.
Any extra regulatory or compliance obligation bolted onto the miscellaneous clauses beyond an NDA's scope.
acceptable_fallbacks: Adding the US e-signature statutory reference (ESIGN + Delaware UETA) — an improvement, not a deviation.
Completed/updated individual identity and notice details (required before signature).
Standard mutual no-waiver / severability language.

positions.title: Entire Agreement and Amendments
positions.standard_position: The Agreement is the final, complete and exclusive agreement of the parties on its subject matter, superseding and merging all prior discussions; no modification or amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of the parties. (Template Clause 14.)
walk_away_triggers: Deleting the written-signed-amendment requirement (allowing oral or course-of-dealing modification).
An integration clause drafted to supersede or subordinate a future definitive consulting/engagement agreement, or to merge away separately negotiated IP/work-product terms.
Incorporating the individual's own standard terms by reference.
acceptable_fallbacks: A carve-out clarifying that the NDA does not supersede any concurrent or future definitive engagement/consulting agreement between the parties (preferred where an engagement is contemplated).
Standard mutual integration language.
